limits: These are direct workload-specific comparisons. Each candidate runs separately; the gains are not additive and do not measure a combined production build.
Two process blocks per arm describe observed variation, not statistical confidence. Desktop activity remained present; builds and our other heavy host work were excluded from clean timing.

Prompt-copy’s new edit gain is about 46%, versus about 28% previously. The difference is localized to verification time, but its cause remains unresolved despite matching acceptance counts, timing boundaries and Metal executable text.
E2 results qualify fresh short prefill. The earlier scalar-decode timing caveat remains; this comparison does not establish zero decode cost.

Prompt-copy covers the four greedy fixtures and a generation-loop seam. Production EOS inside a proposal, stop strings, cancellation, errors, tool turns, sampling and HTTP latency remain outside this qualification.
